recurrence_tracking.pattern_finding: All three recurrences share a common shape: a governance-authorised model extension in wave N whose frozen snapshot is NOT bumped in the SAME commit, discovered N+K waves later when the wave-close cohort finally sees the drifted test. FL-P4-W7-01's twist: the test itself was donor-side (RMS) and hadn't been lifted, so the cohort literally could not have caught it — this is a NEW variant of the class: 'donor-side invariant not yet lifted'. Named as an additional process finding below.

process_finding_extending_FL-P4-W4-01: The DoD ratified at W6 close (contract touch → same-commit snapshot + map + count) does not cover this class-variant. TWO distinct process gaps compound to produce it: (a) 'donor-side invariant not yet lifted' — when any wave adopts a donor module or contract, the wave-close cohort MUST include a lift-check pass that surfaces donor-side invariants for the adopted module; concretely, for each `services/<name>/` or `contracts/<name>.py` newly present, check if the donor repo has a `tests/invariants/test_<name>_*.py` and lift it (or explicitly refuse with a rationale) in the SAME wave close cohort. (b) 'naming-convention blind spot in the grep cohort' — the ratified pattern `test_*_frozen*.py` + `test_*_contract*.py` misses donor-side conventions like `test_<name>_invariants.py` (RMS-IQ-Core-2 uses this). Compensating discipline: extend the wave-close cohort to ALSO grep by CONTENT — any test file whose body contains `model_json_schema()` compared against a `contract_snapshot.json` MUST be in the cohort regardless of filename. Both findings named for W8 opener owner ruling. In the interim: W7 close cohort assemble MUST include content-grep AND every `test_*_invariants.py` file on disk.
